newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Review urges Canberra end Asian radio, TV.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Review urges Canberra end Asian radio, TV.

text.p: A review of the Australian government-owned broadcaster has recommended that it close Radio Australia and perhaps Australian Television International, both services directed at Asia.
The corporation's domestic television services should be largely contracted out, the report recommended.
The Australian Broadcasting Corporation's (ABC) ban on advertising should continue as should its independent news and current affairs services, inquiry chief Bob Mansfield said.

"The ABC should be released from the requirement to operate international broadcasting services and be permitted to direct the resulting savings to its core business of domestic broadcasting," he said.
The corporation should not have to manage the country's main orchestras and they might be moved to local or state control.
It should sell surplus land in its A$345 million portfolio, concentrating on what it needs for broadcasting.

"The ABC should reposition itself as a programme generator for television rather than necessarily a programme maker -- other than in news and current affairs (and where necessary, areas of specialist programming in which the ABC chooses to participate, eg science)," the report said.
"Where programs can be made externally (eg drama and documentaries) this should be encouraged."
Mansfield told reporters that the commission should examine such reforms in the British Broadcasting Corporation.
"Examples like the BBC need to be looked at closely," he said.
Mansfield wanted the ABC to keep the money it saved from shutting Radio Australia and the international television service, if the latter were closed.
But Communications Minister Richard Alston said the government had to consider that as it approached the May budget.

"I have to say, however, that despite that general caveat that I think there is a lot of logic that if the ABC is expected to find A$55 million (its budget target) and it identifies a sum in the order of A$20 million that could be saved from Radio Australia, then those funds ought to be applied in reduction," he said. "So I think the case is a strong one on that front."
The future of the international television service, which broadcasts free-to-air to Asia by satellite, depended on finding someone to operate it commercially, the report said.
"I endorse the government's decision to request the ABC to examine the scope for tendering the operation of Australia Television to the commercial sector," it said.
"If no acceptable commercial relationship is found before June 1997, the service should be closed down."
The corporation should also pare its management.
"The ABC managements ranks should be smaller, with managers assuming increased responsibility and accountability."
The corporation's budget for the year to June is A$531 million, but the current forward estimates show it falling to A$496 million in 1997/98 before rising again thereafter.
However the government is looking for more savings in its May budget.
